raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"From the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, carry on about twelve minutes on foot to the 9/11 Memorial and Museum.","source_id":"GLUE_NAV","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":5},{"text":"Before you head in, look hard at the glass pavilion out front — it leans, on purpose, like a tower knocked onto its side.","source_id":"b2f75c3c-b13e-4f67-83c9-5865e000b11c","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"Above ground, the eight-acre Memorial Plaza is built around the one-acre footprints of both towers, and if you're short on time, that's the part to walk — either way, reserve your tickets online first to skip some of the line at this sobering place.","source_id":"ba7adfa8-381e-41c5-9716-91c1610668b9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"Most museums send you up.","source_id":"73bb9e51-a069-48c8-aa60-109e2904fb70","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"After a thorough security check, this one takes you down, down, down, because the whole museum lives underground — a descent meant to echo the escape route survivors took by stair, and the darkness the attacks plunged the country into.","source_id":"73bb9e51-a069-48c8-aa60-109e2904fb70","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"On the way down the escalator you pass beneath two steel tridents pulled from the bedrock at the base of the North Tower, each one weighing fifty tons.","source_id":"b2f75c3c-b13e-4f67-83c9-5865e000b11c","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"They once helped the towers soar more than 1,360 feet, and when everything else came down, they stayed standing in the sea of rubble — instant symbols of resilience.","source_id":"b2f75c3c-b13e-4f67-83c9-5865e000b11c","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"At the bottom of the last staircase, oddly to the left when everyone wants to turn right, is the museum's beating heart — its history exhibition.","source_id":"73bb9e51-a069-48c8-aa60-109e2904fb70","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"It mixes video, survivor audio, and wall text with artifacts you won't shake: burnt-edged papers that fluttered from the towers, children's clothing recovered from Flight 93.","source_id":"73bb9e51-a069-48c8-aa60-109e2904fb70","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"Among more than 10,300 objects here are the Vesey Street Stairs, dubbed the Survivors' Staircase, which let hundreds of workers flee the site that morning — and a remnant of them sits right beside the museum's own staircase.","source_id":"b2f75c3c-b13e-4f67-83c9-5865e000b11c","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5,"also_cites":["73bb9e51-a069-48c8-aa60-109e2904fb70"]},{"text":"At the foot of that staircase is the In Memoriam gallery, its walls lined with the photographs and names of everyone who perished.","source_id":"52f524f4-ef0c-415c-8ef4-58e0e73214ad","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"Around the corner stands the burnt-out cab of the Fire Department's Engine Company 21, one of the largest artifacts on display — a blunt measure of the inferno the responders walked into.","source_id":"b4bab136-5302-42b7-ac1e-2d33db9b8e01","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"It marks the entrance to the main exhibition, split into three parts: Events of the Day, Before 9/11, and After 9/11.","source_id":"b4bab136-5302-42b7-ac1e-2d33db9b8e01","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"That exhibition spills into the monumental Foundation Hall, where a massive section of the original slurry wall — built to hold back the Hudson while the towers rose — still stands.","source_id":"b4bab136-5302-42b7-ac1e-2d33db9b8e01","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"Beside it is the last steel column removed during the cleanup, covered in messages and mementos left by recovery workers, first responders, and loved ones.","source_id":"b4bab136-5302-42b7-ac1e-2d33db9b8e01","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"Nearby you'll find the Ground Zero cross — a severed chunk of beams that fell by accident into the shape of a cross — alongside a fire truck crushed flat.","source_id":"c7f7e5de-3e10-478d-ae90-8d16aa5f5dd6","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"One thought-provoking section traces the rise of Al Qaeda, down to a single brick from Bin Laden's compound in Abbottabad.","source_id":"c7f7e5de-3e10-478d-ae90-8d16aa5f5dd6","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"And the Memorial Room does something quieter and harder — it shows the face and tells the story of every single person who died.","source_id":"c7f7e5de-3e10-478d-ae90-8d16aa5f5dd6","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"One of those stories sits in a dust-covered wallet that belonged to Robert Joseph Gschaar, an insurance underwriter who worked on the 92nd floor of the South Tower.","source_id":"52f524f4-ef0c-415c-8ef4-58e0e73214ad","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"Inside were a photo of his wife, Myrta, and a two-dollar bill — because when he proposed, a second marriage for them both, he gave her a two-dollar bill as a symbol of their second chance at happiness, and kept the matching one for himself.","source_id":"52f524f4-ef0c-415c-8ef4-58e0e73214ad","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"When you climb back into the light, look for the Oculus, Santiago Calatrava's dramatic white structure over the new WTC Transportation Hub, said to be inspired by a dove taking flight.","source_id":"c78224c8-ec60-4076-843a-00a0496be148","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"Built from 36,500 tons of steel, it streams daylight into a 3.9-billion-dollar station that moves 250,000 train commuters a day, two and a half times the size of Grand Central, with levels of shops and restaurants.","source_id":"c78224c8-ec60-4076-843a-00a0496be148","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5},{"text":"And every September 11, its central skylight is opened for 102 minutes — the exact stretch of time from the first attack to the collapse of the second tower.","source_id":"c78224c8-ec60-4076-843a-00a0496be148","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":5}]}
